newsitem.title: USA: Rolls-Royce speeds up new Trent 800 engines.
newsitem.headline: Rolls-Royce speeds up new Trent 800 engines.

text.p: Rolls-Royce Plc said Friday it has agreed with Boeing Co to bring forward the service-entry date for a 102,000 pound version of the Trent 800 engine for the latest long-haul Boeing 777 airliner, the 200X/300X.

The Trent 8102 will be certified in April 2000 and ready to enter service in January 2001, Rolls-Royce said in a statement that did not say when the engine had previously been expected to be in service. It explained the accelerated development
program is possible because of the high level of commonality with existing Trent 800 variants.
Boeing spokeswoman Ida Hawkins said the 777's using the new Rolls-Royce engine had been scheduled to enter service in September 2001.

Since customers who had selected the Rolls engine wanted an earlier service date, a memorandum of understanding was reached with the engine maker two weeks ago to bring forward the service-entry date to January, she explained.
Trent 800 holds 33 percent of the world market, and has secured all the engine business for Boeing 777s in Southeast Asia, with 50 percent of this market in the Asia-Pacific region, Rolls-Royce said.
